# phase-117 — Let the user pick the REPL theme instead of hardcoding one palette

<!-- GENERATED by rbops/gen-prompts.sh from rbops/phases.json. DO NOT EDIT. -->

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | `minor` |
| Risk | `low` |
| Depends on | _none_ |
| Timeout | 120 min |

## Evidence — verified finding

```
Colour is decided entirely by the implementation. src/repl/style.rs maps each Paint role to one hardcoded SGR - Prompt is 1;34, Heading 1;36, Result 0;32, Error 0;31, Dim 2;37 - and there is no way to change any of it. A user on a light terminal background, or anyone who finds green results unreadable, cannot adjust it. Ipp exposes `.theme` and `.themes` (ipp/main.py, and its REPL_AUDIT.md section 2.39) and that is the single most requested difference found by comparing the two REPLs: of ~35 commands Ipp has that Redblue lacks, theming is the only one that changes what every session looks like. The palette is also scattered across the `sgr()` match rather than held in one named theme value, so 'change the colour of errors' currently means editing a match arm.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Introduce a named theme holding one colour per Paint role, ship two or three themes (a dark-terminal default, a light-terminal variant, and a no-colour theme that behaves exactly as colour-off does today), and add `.themes` to list them and `:theme <name>` to switch at runtime. Switching must take effect immediately with no restart and must not alter any byte of output when the chosen theme is the no-colour one. Do not add per-role overrides — a user who wants one role changed should be able to reach it, but the first version is whole themes, because a partial theme is how a palette becomes incoherent.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `:themes` lists every shipped theme by name with a sample of each colour, and the sample is rendered through the real Style rather than printed literally
- [ ] `:theme <name>` switches at runtime and the very next line's output uses it, with no restart
- [ ] an unknown theme name raises a catchable error naming the available themes, not silently keeping the old one
- [ ] the no-colour theme produces output byte-identical to Style::forced(false) — asserted by comparing bytes, not by eye
- [ ] the palette lives in one theme value rather than in the `sgr()` match arm, so adding a theme is adding a value and not editing a match
- [ ] switching to an unknown or no-colour theme mid-session leaves the session usable - a following program still runs and still prints normally
- [ ] every shipped theme passes the existing repl_color_test suite unchanged, which is the point: colour is now data and the guarantees must not move
- [ ] a test asserts the theme name is resolved case-insensitively and tolerates surrounding whitespace, since it is typed by a human
- [ ] SPEC.md and README.md document the themes and the command; a test asserts every documented theme name actually resolves
